plan: This is a second-price auction (Vickrey-style): I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy — it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bidding behavior. Bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $30, I will bid exactly $30 to ensure optimal outcomes in this one-shot auction.

This is a second-price auction (highest bid wins, pays second-highest bid). In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. Bidding my true value of $7 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade my bid since the payment mechanism already protects me from overpaying.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this setup, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay less than my value in that case, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I should win. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $36.
